answer: Each identity must complete a Wesolowski VDF: repeated modular squaring depends on the prior result, imposing sequential delay that GPUs cannot shorten within one evaluation. An attacker may compute clone proofs in parallel, but needs separate resources and each still incurs the configured wait; this raises the cost of mass Sybil identities rather than making parallelism impossible. A wharf, canyon, or karst offers no shortcut: verification checks each proof.
